reading: Each green box has a one-cell stub on one side. A copy of the box is reflected away from the stub, across the line one cell past the box's far side. The copy is colour 1 when the reflection is left/right and colour 8 when it is up/down.

slots.subject: each green object (box plus one-cell stub)
slots.axis: the row or column just beyond the side of the box opposite the stub
slots.colour: 1 for a horizontal reflection, 8 for a vertical one

why: each copy is the mirror image of its object about that line; the original objects stay

reading: The grid is split into large single-colour regions, with scattered single cells of one noise colour. The output is a 1x1 grid holding the colour of the region that contains the most noise cells.

slots.noise: isolated cells of the one minority colour
slots.answer: colour of the region with the most noise cells, as a 1x1 grid

why: on every pair the output colour is the region with the highest noise count

reading: Scattered single cells are erased. The interior of each rectangular outline is filled with a checkerboard that starts at its top-left interior cell. The checkerboard colour is the scattered colour whose cell count equals the number of checker cells in that interior.

slots.pattern: checkerboard in the interior, top-left interior cell coloured
slots.colour: the scattered marker colour whose count equals that frame's checker cell count

why: marker count of the chosen colour equals checker cells per frame; outlines unchanged

reading: A single 1 sits in the bottom-left corner. A diagonal line of 1 runs up from it, bouncing between the left and right borders all the way to the top, and every other cell becomes 8.

slots.start: the one 1 cell at the bottom-left
slots.path: diagonal going up, reflecting off the side borders

why: one path cell per row, moving one column per row and reversing at the borders

reading: A 3x3 key pattern sits in the top-left corner, framed by a line of 5s. Elsewhere in the noisy grid the same 3x3 pattern appears once, and a 5x5 outline of 5 is drawn around it, overwriting its ring of cells.

slots.key: the top-left 3x3 block inside the 5 corner bracket
slots.match: the other place where the same 3x3 pattern occurs
slots.mark: 5x5 square outline of colour 5 around the match

why: the framed 3x3 equals the key cell for cell; nothing else changes
invariants: all cells outside the new outline unchanged

reading: The grid is made of full-width or full-height colour stripes sprinkled with noise. Every stripe is repainted entirely in its majority colour.

slots.stripes: maximal bands of rows (or columns) sharing one majority colour

why: each output stripe is uniform and equals the input stripe's majority colour
invariants: stripe boundaries and grid size unchanged

reading: A column of 5 splits the grid into two halves. The right half is folded onto the left half (mirrored about the 5 column) and the two are overlaid. The output is the left half alone.
why: the output cell is the left cell or, failing that, the mirrored right cell; the two never conflict

reading: A 1 region sits above a 6 region with a jagged boundary. In the column where 6 reaches highest, a 4 line is drawn from the top 1 row down to the 6. In the column where 1 reaches deepest, a 9 line is drawn from the top 1 row down to the bottom of that 1 run.

slots.peak: column whose 6 reaches the highest row (ties went to the rightmost)
slots.valley: column whose 1 run reaches the lowest row
slots.colours: 4 on the peak column's 1 cells, 9 on the valley column's 1 cells

why: only the 1 cells of those two columns change

reading: A small shape of 2 sits in a noisy 0/5 grid. Copies of that shape are painted in 2 at other places where it fits entirely on 0 cells. Not every fitting spot is used, and the rule that picks the spots is unclear.

slots.targets: selected placements where every cell of the shape lands on 0 (selection rule uncertain)

why: each new 2 group is a translated copy of the original shape on former 0 cells

reading: Each green rectangle sends out two diagonal chains of copies of itself, one down-left and one down-right. Each copy is offset by one block height down and one block width sideways, and the chains continue until they leave the grid.
why: every copy is identical to its source block; the originals stay
